title: Cross-Doc Morphs, Justified Photos, Text-in-Shape, Pull & Tree
description: Five structural patterns: a real multi-page navigation that morphs anyway, a genuine photo-wall packing algorithm, text poured into a silhouette, a hand-built pull-to-refresh, and a keyboard-native tree view.

drops.title: Cross-Document View Transitions
drops.description: Click a sleeve and the whole page navigates for real — yet the artwork morphs seamlessly into the next document's hero.
drops.concept: The CSS Working Group's Cross-Document View Transitions let two entirely separate HTML pages share an animated morph across a real browser navigation, not a same-document SPA route. Each page declares @view-transition { navigation: auto; } and tags the corresponding elements with matching view-transition-name values; the browser captures the old page's final frame, the new page's first frame, and cross-fades/transforms between them automatically. This demo builds five 'sleeve' cards linking to five real static detail pages, each sharing its artwork's view-transition-name with the list — no JavaScript drives the animation at all, and unsupported browsers just get an instant normal navigation.
drops.source: CSS Working Group / web.dev — Cross-Document View Transitions specification

interaction.mouse: Click any sleeve to navigate to its real detail page
interaction.click: Use Previous/Next on a detail page to keep navigating and watch the morph repeat
interaction.touch: Tap a sleeve; swipe-equivalent Previous/Next links on the detail page

drops.title: Justified Photo Wall
drops.description: Twenty-four photos with real, varied aspect ratios pack into perfectly justified rows — the Flickr/Google Photos algorithm, not CSS masonry.
drops.concept: Unlike CSS masonry or bento grids (which pack by column), a justified gallery packs by row: it walks through photos accumulating their aspect ratios until a row would exceed the container width at a target height, then rescales that whole row's height so its total width lands exactly on the container edge. Every tile keeps its true aspect ratio; only the shared row height changes. This demo generates 24 procedurally-textured 'photos' (canvas gradients, no external images) with genuinely varied aspect ratios and reflows them live as you drag the target row height and gap sliders.

interaction.mouse: Drag the row-height and gap sliders; click a tile to open it
interaction.click: Click any tile for a lightbox view; click outside or × to close
interaction.touch: Tap a tile to open, tap outside to dismiss

drops.title: Text-in-Shape Poster
drops.description: A whole paragraph poured inside a heart, star, circle, or drop — not wrapped around it, living inside it, justified line by line.
drops.concept: CSS shape-outside wraps text around a shape's exterior; this does the opposite. A silhouette is rasterized onto an offscreen canvas, then for every text line's y-position, the mask is scanned pixel-by-pixel to find the opaque span's left and right edges. Words are greedily packed into that exact span, and — except on the last line of the paragraph — the leftover space is distributed across word gaps so the line justifies flush to both edges of the silhouette at that height, the same way hand-set silhouette poems worked before computers, just automated at 60 scans a second.
drops.source: Classic hand-typeset 'shape poem' / silhouette typesetting technique

interaction.mouse: Pick a shape, drag line-height/font-size sliders
interaction.click: "New text" cycles the paragraph poured into the shape

drops.title: Custom Pull-to-Refresh
drops.description: Drag a feed down past its own top and feel real elastic resistance, a spinner that spins with your finger, and a genuine release threshold.
drops.concept: Native apps get this gesture for free from the OS; on the web it's hand-rolled: a pointerdown is only armed when scrollTop is already 0, then pointermove converts the raw drag distance into a damped 'pull' value (linear resistance factor, tunable) that drives the spinner's height, rotation, and opacity in real time. Only if the release happens past a real pixel threshold does a refresh actually fire — dragging back up early cancels cleanly with a spring-back transition, exactly like the feed apps this imitates.
drops.source: Pattern behind native pull-to-refresh feeds (Twitter/X, Instagram, Mail apps)

interaction.mouse: Click-drag down from the top of the feed past the threshold, then release
interaction.click: N/A — this is a drag gesture
interaction.touch: Pull down from the top of the list; release past the spinner threshold to refresh

drops.title: Keyboard Tree View
drops.description: A file-explorer sidebar where the whole tree is one Tab stop, and the arrow keys walk, expand, and collapse it like a native OS tree.
drops.concept: Real accessible trees use roving tabindex: only the currently-active row has tabindex=0 (everything else is -1), so Tab moves focus in and out of the whole widget in one stop instead of stepping through every node. Arrow Down/Up move between currently-visible rows; Arrow Right expands a closed folder or, if already open, steps into its first child; Arrow Left collapses an open folder or jumps focus to its parent; Home/End jump to the first/last visible row — the same keyboard model VS Code's and Figma's sidebars use.
drops.source: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices — Tree View Pattern (roving tabindex)

interaction.mouse: Click any row to expand/collapse it
interaction.click: Click a folder row to toggle it open/closed
